matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old `GET /pulls/:id` handler attempted a live GitHub fetch and fell back to stored data on failure. The new handler (lines 203–290) removes the GitHub call entirely and always returns whatever is in the database. Any existing caller that relied on the side effect of refreshing PR data on every GET will now silently receive stale data. The response shape is unchanged, so no immediate failure occurs, but the contract narrows what callers can depend on. The PR description frames this as intentional, but external consumers (e.g., CI runners, integrations) that called this endpoint expecting fresh data will behave differently without any schema-level signal.

findings.title: POST /pulls/:id/refresh lacks error handling for GitHub failures
findings.rationale: The new `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` handler (lines 290–330) calls `gh.getPullRequest` without a try-catch. If GitHub is unreachable, rate-limited, or returns an error, the request will throw and Fastify will return a generic 500 error. The old GET handler had a try-catch that logged a warning and served stale data gracefully. While this is a new endpoint and no existing caller depends on it, a failing refresh could leave the user with no feedback (the client's `useRefreshPull` mutation will catch the error but the UI does not display it). Consider wrapping the GitHub call in a try-catch and returning a partial response or a specific error code so the client can show a meaningful message.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: Previously, GET /pulls/:id attempted to fetch fresh files/commits/body from GitHub and persisted them, falling back to the database on failure. Now it always serves from the database without any GitHub call. Any caller (e.g., an external consumer, e2e test, or CI runner) that relied on GET to get fresh data will now silently receive stale data. The response schema is unchanged, so the caller does not fail, but the behavior is different. The compatible alternative is to keep the old behavior as an option (e.g., a query parameter `?refresh=true`) or document that callers must use POST /pulls/:id/refresh for fresh data.

findings.title: useRefreshPull hook does not guard against null/undefined prId
findings.rationale: The `useRefreshPull` hook accepts `prId: string | null | undefined` and uses it directly in the mutation function URL: `/pulls/${prId}/refresh`. If called with null or undefined, the request would go to `/pulls/null/refresh` or `/pulls/undefined/refresh`, resulting in a 404 or unexpected behavior. While the component guards against this (the button is disabled when prId is falsy and the onClick checks prId), the hook itself is not defensive. This is a hygiene issue that could cause hard-to-debug errors if the hook is reused elsewhere.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer checks that the repo exists
findings.rationale: The old GET handler fetched the repo and threw NotFoundError if it was missing. The new handler removes that check entirely. A caller that relied on a 404 for a PR whose repo was deleted now gets a 200 with stale data. This narrows what callers can depend on.

findings.title: New POST /pulls/:id/refresh endpoint missing response schema
findings.rationale: The new POST route declares `{ schema: { params: IdParams } }` but omits a response schema. While not breaking, adding a response schema (e.g., `response: { 200: PrDetail }`) would enable Fastify's response validation and keep the route consistent with the rest of the codebase.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id response shape narrowed — fields from GitHub API no longer returned

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape narrowed — fields from GitHub API no longer returned
findings.rationale: The old GET route returned `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` when GitHub was reachable, where `detail` came from `gh.getPullRequest` and could include fields such as `state`, `mergeable`, or extra file/commit properties (e.g. `status`, `blob_url`). The new GET always returns the DB-only shape (lines 210–228), which is a strict subset. Any caller that relied on a field present only in the GitHub payload now receives `undefined` for that field. The PR description frames this as intentional, but it is a narrowing of the contract that could silently break a deployed caller that does not update its code. The compatible alternative is to keep the old fields in the GET response (even if stale) or to document the removal in a changelog and version the endpoint.
